main_text.p: quis tristetur objacturam rerum pretiosarum. Porro metus & tristitia in corde sunt affectus appetitus: quia tamen est sympathia appetitui cū facultate cogitante, & imaginante; fit simul imaginatione cerebri sequatur affectus cordis. Est vero triplex, quæ vitio solius capitis fit, melancholia per essentiam dicitur: at quæ fit ob melancholiam in toto corpore redundantem; aut flatus hypochondriorum, est per consensum. De hypochōdriacâ hac disputant artis progeneres; quod tamen persequi, instituti operis brevitas non permittit.

Mania est desipientia cum exandescentiâ sine febre, à calida cerebri intemperie sine tumore. Maniaci aliter sunt affecti quam melancholici, nec metuunt, nec tristantur; sed audaces, temerarii, obvia quæque raptantes.
Vertigo est falsa conversionis imaginatio, una cum lasione voluntarii motus; oriunda in cerebro ex vitiato motu spiritus animi-

page.notes: The first word of the page is partly hidden by the left edge of the scan; "quis" is read from the visible letters, with the start of the word lost. The word "progeneres" is a printing error for "professores"-like forms as printed; it is copied as the scan shows it. The word "oriunda" in the last line is partly obscured and is a doubtful reading. The final word "animi-" is cut at the foot of the page; the rest continues on the next page.
